## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Móténg nǚ jīng* (T551) is a one-fascicle short sūtra by Ān Shìgāo 安世高 ([安世高](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%89%E4%B8%96%E9%AB%98)). The protagonist *Móténg nǚ* 摩鄧女 (the Mātaṅga woman) is the famous low-caste woman whose attempted seduction of Ānanda triggers the discourse in the *Shǒulèngyán jīng* 首楞嚴經 ([KR6j0118](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0118), *Śūraṃgama-sūtra*, T945). This text preserves a much shorter, narrative-focused version of the same story.

**Abstract**

This text opens the "women's sūtras" sub-cycle ([KR6i0182](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0182)–0202) — short narratives centered on female protagonists. The Mātaṅga story illustrates the Buddhist principle that the low-caste woman is no different from any other in her potential for liberation; her devotion to Ānanda is reframed by the Buddha as her aspiration for the Dharma. Translation falls within Ān Shìgāo's productive period (148–170 CE).
